papers.title: BLEnD: A Benchmark for LLMs on Everyday Knowledge in Diverse Cultures and Languages
KoBBQ: Korean Bias Benchmark for Question Answering
Exploring Cross-Cultural Differences in English Hate Speech Annotations: From Dataset Construction to Analysis (CREHate; cited elsewhere as 'Hate Speech Classifiers are Culturally Insensitive')
CORAL: Adaptive Retrieval Loop for Culturally-Aligned Multilingual RAG
FINEST: Improving LLM Responses to Sensitive Topics Through Fine-Grained Evaluation

coauthors.name: Alice Oh
coauthors.relevance_evidence: Senior author on BLEnD, KoBBQ, CREHate and FINEST. BLEnD is 'a hand-crafted benchmark designed to evaluate LLMs' everyday knowledge across diverse cultures and languages'; she leads the KAIST group whose agenda is culture-specific evaluation of LLMs.

coauthors.name: Junho Myung
coauthors.relevance_evidence: Co-first author of BLEnD, which shows 'LLMs perform better for cultures that are highly represented online, with a maximum 57.34% difference in GPT-4'; also co-author of CREHate on cross-cultural hate speech annotation.

coauthors.name: Yi Zhou
coauthors.relevance_evidence: Co-first author of BLEnD, a benchmark for 'culture-specific knowledge of daily life, especially across diverse regions and non-English languages' in LLMs.

coauthors.name: Jiho Jin
coauthors.relevance_evidence: First author of KoBBQ, which builds 'social biases reflecting Korean culture' into a bias benchmark; also co-author of BLEnD and CREHate.

coauthors.name: Hwaran Lee
coauthors.relevance_evidence: Senior author of KoBBQ, a Korean-culture-specific bias benchmark that contrasts native Korean templates against 'machine-translated versions of BBQ', i.e. cultural localization of value/bias evaluation; also co-author of BLEnD.

coauthors.name: Jiseon Kim
coauthors.relevance_evidence: KoBBQ co-author (Korean cultural stereotypes in LLM QA) and author of 'Exploring Persona-dependent LLM Alignment for the Moral Machine Experiment' and 'Machine Behavior in Relational Moral Dilemmas' - directly about moral values and value alignment in LLMs.

coauthors.name: Haneul Yoo
coauthors.relevance_evidence: KoBBQ co-author; KoBBQ is a culturally localized Korean bias benchmark rather than a translation of the English BBQ, addressing culture-specific stereotypes in LLMs.

coauthors.name: Chani Jung
coauthors.relevance_evidence: Co-first author of CREHate: 'Most hate speech datasets neglect the cultural diversity within a single language'; the paper finds 'only 59.4% of the samples achieving consensus among all countries', a direct cross-cultural values finding.

coauthors.name: Juho Kim
coauthors.relevance_evidence: CREHate co-author; the paper's 'analysis highlights statistically significant differences based on nationality' in hate speech judgments - cross-cultural disagreement in annotation of offensive content.

coauthors.name: Jose Camacho-Collados
coauthors.relevance_evidence: Co-author of both CREHate (cross-cultural English hate speech re-annotation across five countries) and BLEnD (everyday cultural knowledge in LLMs across 16 countries/regions).

coauthors.name: Rifki Afina Putri
coauthors.relevance_evidence: BLEnD co-author; BLEnD covers 'low-resource ones such as Amharic, Assamese, Azerbaijani, Hausa, and Sundanese' and measures LLM failures on underrepresented cultures' everyday knowledge.

coauthors.name: Eunsu Kim
coauthors.relevance_evidence: BLEnD co-author on a benchmark whose premise is that LLMs are 'primarily trained on English data reflecting Western perspectives' and therefore misrepresent non-Western cultures.

coauthors.name: Kiwoong Park
coauthors.relevance_evidence: BLEnD co-author/annotator on the cultural everyday-knowledge benchmark spanning 16 countries and 13 languages.

coauthors.name: Anar Sabuhi Rzayev
coauthors.relevance_evidence: BLEnD is his only arXiv work, and it is squarely a cultural benchmark: 'LLMs often lack culture-specific knowledge of daily life, especially across diverse regions and non-English languages.'

coauthors.name: Dimosthenis Antypas
coauthors.relevance_evidence: BLEnD co-author; the benchmark quantifies cross-cultural performance gaps in LLMs (e.g. 'maximum 57.34% difference in GPT-4').

coauthors.name: Hsuvas Borkakoty
coauthors.relevance_evidence: BLEnD co-author on the hand-crafted 52.6k-pair benchmark of culture-specific everyday knowledge for LLMs.

coauthors.name: Carla Perez-Almendros
coauthors.relevance_evidence: BLEnD co-author, and author of 'Why are all LLMs Obsessed with Japanese Culture? On the Hidden Cultural and Regional Biases of LLMs' and 'SemEval-2026 Task 7: Everyday Knowledge Across Diverse Languages and Cultures' - explicit cultural-bias work on LLMs.

coauthors.name: Nina White
coauthors.relevance_evidence: BLEnD is her only arXiv work; it evaluates 'LLMs' everyday knowledge across diverse cultures and languages' with human annotators from 16 countries/regions.

coauthors.name: Nedjma Ousidhoum
coauthors.relevance_evidence: BLEnD co-author; the paper argues culturally unaware LLM outputs 'can lead to hallucinations or stereotypical responses, potentially offending a large and diverse user base.'

coauthors.name: Mohammad Taher Pilehvar
coauthors.relevance_evidence: BLEnD co-author on the cross-cultural everyday-knowledge benchmark for LLMs covering 13 languages including low-resource ones.

coauthors.name: Victor Gutierrez-Basulto
coauthors.relevance_evidence: Qualifies via BLEnD only (his other arXiv work is description logics): BLEnD is 'a benchmark designed to evaluate LLMs' everyday knowledge across diverse cultures and languages.'

coauthors.name: Yazmin Ibanez-Garcia
coauthors.relevance_evidence: Qualifies via BLEnD only (her other arXiv work is ontologies/query answering): BLEnD measures LLM cultural knowledge gaps across 16 countries/regions.

coauthors.name: Abinew Ali Ayele
coauthors.relevance_evidence: BLEnD co-author responsible for underrepresented-culture coverage; the benchmark explicitly targets low-resource cultures such as Amharic-speaking Ethiopia.

coauthors.name: Seid Muhie Yimam
coauthors.relevance_evidence: BLEnD co-author; contributes to the benchmark's claim that 'for cultures represented by low-resource languages, LLMs perform better in English than the local languages.'

coauthors.name: Shamsuddeen Hassan Muhammad
coauthors.relevance_evidence: BLEnD co-author covering Hausa; the paper documents LLMs' systematically worse everyday-cultural knowledge for underrepresented regions.

coauthors.name: Juhyun Oh
coauthors.relevance_evidence: First author of FINEST, and author of 'Culture is Everywhere: A Call for Intentionally Cultural Evaluation' and 'JuICE: A Benchmark for Evaluating LLM-Judge in Identifying Cultural Errors' - directly about cultural evaluation of LLMs.

coauthors.name: Jiwoo Song
coauthors.relevance_evidence: Co-author of CORAL, which introduces retrieval that critiques 'evidence for relevance and cultural alignment' because fixed-space mRAG 'may be inadequate for culturally grounded queries' - value/culture localization in LLM pipelines.

coauthors.name: Byeongcheol Kang
coauthors.relevance_evidence: Co-author of CORAL, an adaptive multilingual RAG method evaluated 'across two cultural QA benchmarks' and designed to produce 'culturally relevant answers'.

coauthors.name: Jongwon Lee
coauthors.relevance_evidence: Only shared work is FINEST, a fine-grained safety/helpfulness evaluation taxonomy for sensitive topics with no cultural-values dimension; the arXiv name is also shared with robotics and physics namesakes. No culture or value-alignment work verified.

coauthors.name: Taeui Song
coauthors.relevance_evidence: FINEST is the only arXiv work under this name, and it concerns 'overly cautious and vague responses on sensitive topics' (safety vs helpfulness), not culture, cross-cultural difference or value alignment.
